knowledge.purpose: Terms and what they mean, as a real <dl>: a glossary, a spec sheet, the key facts of a record (term, then one or more descriptions).
useCases: Glossary of terms on a documentation page
Product spec sheet: Weight 1.2 kg, Battery 12 hours
Key facts of an order or a booking: Date, Guests, Table
antiPatterns: Rows with several comparable columns: use data.table
Questions with answers the visitor opens one by one: use container.accordion (openAll for a list read top to bottom)
A plain list of items with no terms: use data.list
knowledge.implementation: `items` is a list of {term, description}; a description may be a string or a list of strings (several <dd> under one term). layout "stacked" puts each description under its term; "columns" puts the term beside its description in a two-column grid that stacks below 420px of the block's own width. `dividers` draws a rule between pairs. Each pair is wrapped in a <div>, which is valid inside <dl>. Items without a term are skipped; with no items the block draws nothing.

jsonSchema.description: The pairs: a term and its description (or several descriptions).
stacked: each description under its term. columns: the term beside its description; stacks on a narrow box.
